claims: There are four identical ROMs in the architecture.
The initializations of the ROMs are identical.
Each ROM has distinct read addresses.
The write clocks for all ROMs are constantly zero.
The write enables for all ROMs are constantly one.
The busy signal directly aliases the LED signal.
The total count of flip-flops is 71.

architectural_interpretations.hypothesis: The four ROMs suggest a multi-byte iterative datapath due to their identical configurations and distinct read addresses.
falsification_tests: Analyze if any two ROMs serve identical functions under variable conditions.
Verify if read addresses lead to consistent outputs across iterations.

architectural_interpretations.hypothesis: The interconnections between ROM outputs and registers indicate data flow that is meant for iterative processing.
falsification_tests: Trace output paths to see if they are used in feedback loops.
Check if register outputs have dependencies on previous state data.

unknowns: The specific function of the cipher being implemented is not known.
The criteria for mode selection or switching between functions remains unclear.
Final output generation logic or its relationship to previous processing stages is not established.

next_steps.experiment: Map the interconnections of the outputs from each ROM to their respective registers, aiming to visualize data dependencies and the flow of data.
next_steps.description: Identify how outputs are combined and whether they influence each other’s read patterns.

next_steps.experiment: Test mode selection behavior by simulating various control signal conditions (e.g., pin_25 for ENC_DEC) and observing resultant changes in signal outputs, primarily related to final output modes.
next_steps.description: Investigate how mode signals affect data flow and confirm the hypothesis on multiple operational states for the cipher.
